The core operators derive from a synthesis of Gestalt theory and purposive behaviorism. Sign gestalt expectation encapsulates how perception integrates into anticipatory structures, forming the basis of mnemonization. Means-end expectations provide a mechanism for goal-directed action selection, rooted in the principle of least effort. Laws of purposive behaviorism unify these into a dynamic system where capacity and stimulus interact to produce adaptive behavior. These primitives form a closed-loop system: perception generates expectations, which guide action, and outcomes update expectations—creating a recursive feedback architecture. Dualities emerge in the tension between internal capacity and external constraint, and between immediate reward and long-term goal alignment. Failure modes include perceptual overload, expectation mismatch, and capacity depletion. The mathematical structure supports both Bayesian inference in GSI and state-transition modeling in GSE.
